analyzed_vuln.description: Heap-use-after-free is caused by incorrect AST surgery in yr_re_ast_split_at_chaining_point. When splitting a concat AST at an ungreedy large range node, it detaches siblings around `child` but does not update `re_ast->root_node->children_head` when `child` is the first child. It then calls `yr_re_node_destroy(child)`, freeing that node, while the original AST root still points to it as head. Later, parser cleanup calls `yr_re_ast_destroy(re_ast)` -> `yr_re_node_destroy`, which traverses from stale `children_head` and reads the freed node (`child->next_sibling`), triggering UAF at re.c:155.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Triggered via rules_fuzzer parsing a regexp string that causes chaining split, e.g. `rule r{strings:$=/.{,}?/`. Data flow: harness -> yr_lex_parse_rules_string -> grammar/parser -> yr_parser_reduce_string_declaration parses regexp AST and repeatedly calls yr_re_ast_split_at_chaining_point. For a concat where the split point is the first node (`RE_NODE_RANGE_ANY`, non-greedy, large bounds), split function frees that node without fixing head pointer. Subsequent AST destruction in yr_parser_reduce_string_declaration (normal/cleanup path) dereferences freed memory, causing ASan heap-use-after-free.
